provenance_note: The original study_summary.json and study_report.md contain erroneous derived metrics (an invalid cumulative global-time ratio of 0.6784258 and tie-break loss misattribution) and are preserved unmodified for provenance. This corrected document recomputes all summary metrics directly from the raw arm metrics JSON records (arm_*.json) without retraining or modifying raw training data.
execution_notes: Recorded work time is 5679.615209s out of a 6000s ceiling (peak RSS: 309510144 bytes).
The work timer started after initial marker file creation and thread/device setup; it does not certify a literal all-setup-inclusive 100 minutes.
In-flight deadline overruns and partial final validations are honestly retained (no hard-kill enforcement).

Raw test log records 32 tests passing with OK and EXIT_STATUS=0, but lacks timestamp headers and invocation command; two tests (chunked-vs-continuous state equivalence and deadline handling) feature weak assertions that do not compare model states or check individual arm deadline skipping. Testing does not prove pre-run execution order.
Single paired seed (seed 0) across arms with unequal final caps (50000, 41919, 46400, 43886); does not constitute full-paper replication or universal mechanism claims.

crossing_speedups.reason: Neither arm achieved >=0.95 accuracy on full validation within stopping limits (none_wd0 capped at 50,000 updates, ema_wd0 stopped at 41,919 updates with last complete validation at 41,900). Both arms are censored; speedup is not estimable.

crossing_speedups.update_ratio_definition: 5900 / 1200 = 4.9166667. Ratio of updates to first observed full >=0.95 validation accuracy, evaluated on a 100-update grid (not an exact latent crossing time).

rejected_old_work_time_ratio.reason_rejected: REJECTED as invalid. runner.py logged work_elapsed_s measured continuously from GLOBAL study start (clock() - global_start). Because study arms ran sequentially (none_wd0 -> ema_wd0 -> none_wd0.005 -> ema_wd0.005), EMA's timestamp (4217.993s) accumulated the execution duration of all three prior arms (~4179s prior work), while baseline's timestamp (2861.595s) accumulated only the first two arms (~2678s prior work). Dividing these cumulative global timestamps compares non-coincident, offset time spans and produces a meaningless speedup number.

recovered_interval_comparison.inclusions: Intervening training updates, periodic 100-step full validations, evaluation overhead, and disk/checkpoint I/O between step 0 validation END and first >=0.95 validation END.
recovered_interval_comparison.exclusions: Model, data, and optimizer initialization; device/thread setup; and the initial step 0 validation execution.
recovered_interval_comparison.qualifications: Precisely bounded interval from post-initialization validation completion to crossing validation completion. This is NOT a setup-inclusive arm runtime or whole-study speedup. Exact arm-start timestamps were not recorded by runner.py.
